{"sample_id": "blind-8b44e73f9cd844a3b2bd0c09fb7bcf82", "theorem": "Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "number_theory", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "\begin{proof}

    Let $a$ a primitive root modulo $p$.

As $a^{p-1} \equiv 1(\bmod p), p \mid\left(a^{(p-1) / 2}-1\right)\left(a^{(p-1) / 2}+1\right)$, so $p \mid a^{(p-1) / 2}-1$ or $p \mid$ $a^{(p-1) / 2}+1$. As $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p, a^{(p-1) / 2} \not \equiv 1(\bmod p)$, so

$$

a^{(p-1) / 2} \equiv-1 \quad(\bmod p) .

$$

Hence $(-a)^{(p-1) / 2}=(-1)^{2 t+1} a^{(p-1) / 2} \equiv(-1) \times(-1)=1(\bmod p)$.

Suppose that $(-a)^n \equiv 1(\bmod p)$, with $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Then $a^{2 n}=(-a)^{2 n} \equiv 1(\bmod p)$, so $p-1\left|2 n, \frac{p-1}{2}\right| n$.

So $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$ modulo $p$.

Conversely, suppose that $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2=2 t+1$ modulo $p$. Let $2, p_1, \ldots p_k$ the prime factors of $p-1$, where $p_i$ are odd.

$a^{(p-1) / 2}=a^{2 t+1}=-(-a)^{2 t+1}=-(-a)^{(p-1) / 2} \equiv-1$, so $a^{(p-1) / 2} \not \equiv 1(\bmod 2)$.

As $p-1$ is even, $(p-1) / p_i$ is even, so $a^{(p-1) / p_i}=(-a)^{(p-1) / p_i} \not \equiv 1(\bmod p)($ since $-a$ has order $p-1)$.

So the order of $a$ is $p-1$ (see Ex. 4.8) : $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$.

\end{proof}"}

{"sample_id": "blind-4afb0d2f024d414f9fbf9c8553e694e6", "theorem": "Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "topology", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "For each fixed \(x\in[0,1)\), we have \(x^n\to 0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus \((f_n)\) converges pointwise to
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
Suppose the convergence were uniform. Take \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12\). For every positive integer \(N\), let \(n=N\) and \(x=2^{-1/N}\). Then \(x\in[0,1)\), so \(f(x)=0\), but
\[
|f_n(x)-f(x)|=x^N=\frac12.
\]
Hence no \(N\) can ensure \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\tfrac12\) for all \(n\ge N\) and all \(x\in[0,1]\). Therefore \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\)."}

\[
a^2+ab+b^2=\left(a+\frac b2\right)^2+\frac34b^2\ge 0。
\]
若该式等于 0，则 b=0 且 a=0，这与 a<b 矛盾，故 a^2+ab+b^2>0。因此
\[
b^3-a^3=(b-a)(a^2+ab+b^2)>0，
\]
即 a^3<b^3。"}

{"sample_id": "blind-70c5f350fedc45a382e4d096b70a5317", "theorem": "Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "number_theory", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), so \(m\) is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Thus \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\), while \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(p\) is odd, \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Therefore
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
If \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Hence \(2m\mid2n\), so \(m\mid n\). Since \((-a)^m\equiv1\pmod p\), it follows that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\), and put \(x=-a\). Then \(x\) has odd order \(m\), and
\[
a^{2m}=(-x)^{2m}=x^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Suppose \(a^n=(-x)^n\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(n\) were odd, then \(x^n\equiv-1\pmod p\). Squaring gives \(x^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\), which would give \(x^n\equiv1\pmod p\), contradicting \(x^n\equiv-1\pmod p\) because \(p\) is odd. Thus \(n\) is even. Consequently \(x^n=(-x)^n=a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid n\). Since \(m\) is odd and \(n\) is even, \(2m\mid n\). Therefore every positive exponent annihilating \(a\) is divisible by \(2m\), while \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). Hence \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\), so \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\)."}
